- [ ] **finance** — monetary amounts, rates and prices carry `math:Quantity` dimensions; interest/return computations reference `math:` operations.
- [ ] **risk** — risk scores/likelihoods ground in the probability layer (`Prior`/`Posterior` where Bayesian; never bare floats).
- [ ] **quality** — quality metrics as dimensioned quantities; aggregate scores with declared estimators.
- [ ] **evidence / trust** — strength/confidence values ride the probability-vs-confidence never-conflate rule (P19): confidences stay `logic:confidence`, probabilities require a model.
- [ ] **model-serving** — tensors/metrics ground in the linear-algebra layer (`TensorComputationGraph`, `math:LossFunction`).
- [x] ~~**diagnostics** — extend the 3-ref toehold to graded-severity quantities.~~ **Struck: already grounded.**
  `gmeow:gradeOrdinal` embeds each truth-order chain into (ℤ, ≤) — severityInfo 0, Note 1,
  Warning 2, Error 3 — with the one-way bridge `math:integers math:formalizes gmeow:gradeOrdinal`
  declared in the math slice, and the term states it is "the Principle-19 MATH grounding of the
  truth ordering" and "NOT a parallel gmeow:Grade subtree". Severity is ORDINAL, not dimensioned;

Blocked by the probability and statistics layers **only where a cluster needs them** — risk and evidence. finance, quality, model-serving and diagnostics are not blocked and can start now.

- No inherently quantitative slice sits at `math:` 0.
- Each grounded slice records `math:` in its manifest `gmeow:sliceDependsOn` set.

`affect` (38 refs) is the worked precedent. `observations` is the smaller one, and is now complete end to end: it declares `slices/math` in `gmeow:sliceDependsOn`, consumes `math:Quantity`, and its structural tests *assert the legacy `gmeow:` quantity vocabulary is absent* rather than merely not using it — see `slices/core/observations/tests/structural.ttl:136`. ## Proposed solution

One epic, five lanes. Lane 0 is the unifier; A–D are its facets and land against it.

### Lane 0 — Agentic modal kernel (the unifier)

A design doc, peer of `LOGIC-TELEOLOGY.md` (working title `LOGIC-AGENTIC-MODALITY.md`),
defining **composite modal expressions** over the existing typed context algebra: how deontic,
temporal, telic, and protocol contexts nest and commute, which compositions are meaningful,
and the evaluation semantics of a composite expression against an enactment. Every construct
in lanes A–D is specified here first and only *named* in slice vocabularies.

### Lane A — Intent algebra (net-new)

Compositional operators over the existing Desire → Intention → Commitment trichotomy
(`slices/core/teleology`): compose, refine, join/meet under the seven existing goal-conflict
relations, priority, and delegation — **with the algebraic laws stated explicitly**
(associativity, idempotence, absorption; which laws *fail* and why), grounded via
`docs/APPLIED_CATEGORY_THEORY/`. Adds **intention revision** as the conative parallel of the
belief-revision machinery in `slices/core/epistemics`. Reuses `logic:refinesGoal`,
`logic:And/OrDecomposition`, `gmeow:counterGoal`. Authored as EL-safe `logic:` axioms; honest
`logic:expressivenessBoundary` records wherever the algebra exceeds FOL.

### Lane B — Deontic work graphs (per-step)

Extend the enactment kernel + `work-orchestration` binding so deontic modality attaches to
individual `logic:TransactionStep`s and transitions (obligated/permitted/forbidden steps and
edges), reusing the existing `gmeow:DeonticModality` individuals — "deontic work graph"
becomes the named design term. Includes:

- **Contrary-to-duty / reparational obligations** — what is obligated *after* a violation —
  tied to the compensation machinery already in `gmeow:ActionPolicy` and the enactment kernel.
- Violation remains a vantage judgment via `gmeow:ComplianceAssessment` — never entailed
  ("there is no ought, only ought-according-to").
- Counter-example fixtures for the classic deontic paradoxes (Chisholm's contrary-to-duty
  set, Ross's paradox) alongside the existing enactment counter-examples.

### Lane C — Choreography, with orchestration as its projection

Interaction-protocol vocabulary — protocol, protocol role, message exchange,
enactment-of-protocol — built on the Singh commitment machinery already present
(`logic:ApprovalState` detachment lifecycle). Two structural commitments:

- **Hohfeldian dynamics as the bridge to deontics**: a protocol move exercises a *power* that
  creates/discharges obligations, reusing the `rights` graft on `norms`. A choreography IS a
  deontic work graph viewed from all roles at once.
- **Endpoint projection as a theorem, not a taxonomy**: an orchestration is the
  role-projection of a choreography — shipped as a generated projection with an explicit
  preservation judgment in the `graph/correspondence-laws` graph (Principle 17).

External dialects (BSPL, BPMN choreography, WS-CDL) enter only as `logic:` grounding
BridgeViews — never a competing grounding in a domain slice.

### Lane D — Temporal operators, targeted as LTLf

Named `eventually` / `globally` / `until` / `next` operators evaluated over **finite
enactment journals**: `logic:Enactment` is an append-only finite run, so finite-trace LTL
(LTLf) is decidable and slots directly into the declared-decidable-fragment discipline —
full infinite-path LTL gets an honest `logic:expressivenessBoundary` record instead of a
pretend implementation. Operators are explicitly reconciled with the existing goal-expression
kinds (achievement ≙ eventually, maintenance ≙ globally, deadline-window ≙ bounded until):
one temporal truth source, the operators a named surface over it, never a parallel semantics.

### Integration requirements (all lanes)

- Per-step violation/compliance findings route through **DiagLedger** (finding IRI + anchor +
  antecedents) so meta-reasoning over the finding graph works live, not only on fixtures.
- Native-reasoner support per lane in `crates/logic` — vocabulary-only landings do not close
  a lane. Declared dependency: **#1695** (route modal verdict evaluation through the shipped
  reasoner) is a foundational prerequisite for every lane.
- The norms slice's deferred alignments (ODRL 2.2, LegalRuleML, DPV, UFO-L — see
  `slices/core/norms/docs.md`) are folded in where a lane touches them, extending the pinned
  correspondence coverage tests in the same change (Principle 7).
- **Dogfood demonstrator in `examples/`** (not `tests/conformance-fixtures/` — the projection
  universe scans `examples/`): the repo's own working discipline — the CLAUDE.md norms
  ("never rebase", "sync once"), the stage1→3 workflow, the host-global lock as a fairness
  queue — encoded as a deontic work graph. The standing constraints are themselves norms with
  issuers, bearers, and modalities; the ontology should be able to say so.

## Who is the consumer?

- `slices/profile/agent-runtime` — agents reasoning about what they are obligated/permitted
  to do next, per step, under deadline.
- `slices/core/work-orchestration` operator review surfaces — per-step deontic status and
  reparational obligations in the review projection.
- `slices/core/agentic` `gmeow:ActionPolicy` reasoning — permitted-transition semantics for
  tool surfaces gains deontic + temporal composition.
- The `gmeow` CLI agent surface (the shippable deliverable).
- The dogfood demonstrator itself: the repo's own working discipline as shipped ontology
  content (P15's "named user need" made literal).

## Examples or prior art

- In-repo: `LOGIC-SEMANTICS.md` (typed context algebra), `LOGIC-TELEOLOGY.md` (goal kinds,
  deontic force over goals), `LOGIC-ENACTMENT.md` (Singh detachment lifecycle,
  `logic:EffectProtocolPosition`), `slices/core/work-orchestration/design/WORK-ORCHESTRATION.md`,
  the rights graft (`slices/core/rights`).
- External: Singh's commitment machines / BSPL; Hohfeld's jural positions; De Giacomo &
  Vardi's LTLf/LDLf; Chisholm and Ross for the deontic counter-example corpus; UFO-C/UFO-L
  for the intentional-moment and legal-relator groundings.

## Alternatives considered

- **Four independent features** — rejected: without Lane 0 the vocabularies cannot express
  composite modal sentences, which is the actual agent-level requirement.
- **Full LTL over infinite paths** — rejected as the primary target: outside the finite-journal evaluation contract; the append-only enactment journal already chose finite-trace semantics.
- **A choreography DSL alongside orchestration** — rejected: two parallel process vocabularies
  violate the one-truth-source doctrine; endpoint projection makes orchestration derived.
- **Deontic status via hand-authored SHACL on work steps** — forbidden authoring surface;
  validation derives from `logic:` axioms (projection-purity gate).

## Additional context

Authoring constraints: all semantics land as EL-safe `logic:` axioms and
`logic:Constraint`/`logic:Formula` in `module.ttl` files (shapes are derived, never authored);
external formalisms only via `logic:` grounding BridgeViews with correspondence-law rows and
extended pinned coverage tests; Rust-first (no Python); P12 throughout — policies, protocols,
and temporal formulas are carried and reasoned about, **never executed** in CI.

Suggested child-issue split, in dependency order (with #1695 first):

1. Lane 0 kernel design doc + composite-expression vocabulary
2. Lane D — LTLf operators over enactment journals (temporal substrate for B and C)
3. Lane B — per-step deontic work graphs + CTD/reparation + paradox counter-examples
4. Lane C — protocol vocabulary, Hohfeldian powers, endpoint projection
5. Lane A — intent algebra + intention revision (parallel to 2–4)
6. Dogfood demonstrator + DiagLedger routing + deferred norm alignments (closes the epic)

Acceptance criteria per lane: design-doc section merged; vocabulary + EL-safe axioms in the
owning `module.ttl`; native reasoner evaluation in `crates/logic` with conformance fixtures
AND counter-examples; competency queries; `examples/` demonstrator visible to the projection
universe; correspondence rows + coverage-test extension for any external grounding.

## Approved engineering and semantic contract

SOTA and greenfield design direct architecture; ceremony guides implementation. Reuse must earn its place through semantic fit and measured performance. PurRDF is our editable first-party execution/data substrate; GMEOW owns vocabulary, calculus, context and policy. The current dependency choice is `purrdf = "2"` in both manifests. Committed root and fuzz lockfiles select exact PurRDF package versions, registry sources and checksums, and all shipped browser engines must match the selected root substrate. Dependency updates preserve the authored compatibility requirement and rebuild the six browser engines; GMEOW does not rerun upstream conformance. Do not retain weak internal representations merely because they exist.

The complete calculus plus all existing projection targets and both APPLIED_CATEGORY_THEORY worked examples are required. Adapters for every external standard mentioned in the research are not selected. LOGIC-CORRESPONDENCE.md governs take1.md; canonical semantics remain grounding/logic-owned in graph/correspondence-laws. #1712 has a current-code reconciliation and its remaining defects are owned by #1741–#1745, not a revival of the stale branch.

Implement all seven rungs; get:S->V and put:V x S->S with explicit prior state and complements; individual GetPut/PutGet/PutPut/SectionLaw evidence; typed caveats and native fragment/termination admission. Inverse syntax or a boolean never proves recovery. Keep standpoint, source identity, provenance, complete RDF 1.2 statement structure, effects and load-bearing annotations.

Composition computes each axis through canonical logic rules: declared confidence t-norm with explicit independence for product, min evidence, additive weight, model-bound probability, separate determinacy and preservation polarities. Refutation survives composition; absent refutation, unknown prevents discharge. Indexed finite-theory merge has an explicit shared apex, checked embeddings and factorization evidence; contested claims coexist and unsupported general-theory claims remain expressiveness boundaries.

Inventory and remove downstream duplicate tests after identifying their exact upstream owners, while retaining GMEOW-specific calculus, stage, policy and product checks. ## Performance and completion

Batch coherent changes before expensive make check cycles. Use focused owned checks for development, then required gates for the complete batch. Never bypass commit verification.

All production execution and measurements use the authenticated O3/full-LTO producer, including PurRDF dependencies, with tests/debugging built separately. Keep conversion removal, prepared-query/analysis reuse, fusion, incremental maintenance and scheduling observable separately. Retain BOTH independent cold CI generations and exact output comparison. Preserve both commits, its worktree and every existing implementation branch. The eight reports are concrete additional children of this approved implementation, not post-merge follow-ups:

Preserve owned definitions, constraints and obligations in the semantic denominator. Removing a `math:memberCondition` root from assertions supplies no set-builder denotation.
- Bound-term `termEqual`/`termDistinct` comparisons are distinct from denotational `sameAs`/`differentFrom`. No implicit FOL equality/inequality transfer or unique-name assumption is permitted. Expose comparison policy, legal placement, binding, datatype-value and error behavior. The reported implication-consequent `termDistinct` must receive an explicit admission or unsupported disposition; do not rewrite the consumer canon. Whole-source success stays blocked wherever that required transfer is unavailable.
- Literal identity is lexical spelling + effective datatype + normalized language + base direction, across direct, standalone, nested and rule paths. Keep integer lexical variants distinct as terms; test value comparison separately. Plain strings/explicit `xsd:string` and language-tag case are equivalence controls. Quotation never implies assertion.

An inconsistent base does not yield a useful entailment pass. Raw E/SZS observations remain explicitly external diagnostic evidence; independent certificate checking and certified transfer are required for stronger authority.

body:
Drained from the local `.deficiencies` ledger (recorded under #1544, merged as PR 1550). Re-verified against current `main`.

Relates to: #1443 (math expressions hardening — the sibling Rust-validator failure-class work, currently in flight) and #1551 (logic:-only grounding for the math slice).

## Problem

The signed compactified radial field grounding shipped with three disclosed fragment limits and one unregistered facility. Each was an accepted boundary at the time; none is tracked.

### 1. The extended-real gate does not catch a non-numeric literal

`math:ExtendedRealValueConstraint` enforces the non-literal-must-be-a-pole case, but the guarded `logic:` fragment has no numeric-datatype test, so a non-numeric literal in an extended-real position passes.

### 2. Measure non-negativity does not forbid a finite negative

`math:MeasureResultNonNegativeConstraint` forbids the `math:NegativeInfinity` pole but not a finite-negative literal. `logic:ValueRangeConstraint` landed on main after this work, so a tightening is now plausible — but `measureResult` spans literal-or-`PositiveInfinity`, so `sh:minInclusive` is not straightforwardly safe. Needs a design pass, not a one-liner.

### 3. `gmeow:FlagshipScenario` is not registered for the radial scenes

The positive-capability radial scenes are not registered as flagship scenarios: the facility needs a native Rust producer plus a single enforceable hard-rule failure. The scenes carry the full non-flagship test surface instead.

### 4. Three examples ride the non-conformant allowlist

`examples/closed-form-functions`, `signed-radial-field-qualitative`, and `signed-radial-field-closed-form` are on the `example_sweep` `NON_CONFORMANT` allowlist (`crates/validate/tests/example_sweep.rs:44`) for standalone closed-world isolation — the same accepted pattern as ~14 sibling math examples. They conform in the merged bundle (`make validate` clean). Worth revisiting as part of any wider decision about that allowlist, not on its own.

## Two things that are correct as shipped — do not "fix" them

- `math:convexityLaw` is authored as **midpoint** convexity, not the full lambda-chord inequality: the continuum of lambda needs scalar arithmetic beyond the first-order guarded fragment. Disclosed in the law, not faked.
- Closed-form leaf-linkage runtime enforcement is a `tests/structural.ttl` MUST cell over authored instances rather than a live `logic:Constraint`, because transitive AST traversal exceeds the guarded fragment.

## Work

- [ ] Give the extended-real gate a numeric-datatype test, or record why the guarded fragment cannot carry one.
- [ ] Decide how to forbid a finite-negative `measureResult` without breaking the literal-or-pole span.
- [ ] Register the radial scenes as flagship scenarios, or state that the non-flagship surface is sufficient.

Drained from the local `.deficiencies` ledger (recorded 2026-07-14 under the math shape-grounding packet, and under #764, #1374, #1546). Re-verified against current `main`.

Blocked by: #1530 — the slice authoring factory owns the machinery (briefs, fuzzy-gated two-stage translations, distinctiveness guard) that makes this authorable without producing gamed boilerplate.
Relates to: #1642 (the four axis floors this debt currently caps).

## Problem

Four separate landings deliberately shipped vocabulary without its full documentation coat or translations, each with explicit approval at the time. The debt is now the binding constraint on several slice-quality axes, and nothing tracks burning it down.

### 1. The math slice (the largest block)

Excluded from the shape-grounding PR by explicit user direction ("Everything but the translations, we'll punt those for now"):

- ~**691 uncoated terms** across 8 annotation fields.
- ~**1,383 untranslated literals** across 2 languages.

The math slice therefore sits at tier Registered: translation coverage measures **0.41**, information coverage ~**0.60**. The floor was deliberately kept at 0.333 rather than pinned at 0.41, because the sanctioned coat authoring will expand the localizable denominator and a 0.41 pin would manufacture a guaranteed future gate red.

### 2. GMN math-symbology terms in the lang slice

The GMN symbology plane added ~95 new sign-inventory terms to `slices/grounding/lang/module.ttl` (number-type classes, set/order operator families, the extended real line and its poles, and their Form/Denotation records). Only **19** received authored fr + cmn translations — the number sufficient to restore the lang `axisTranslationCoverage` floor after the additions widened the localizable set. **~76 carry English labels/definitions with no translation.**

The `.po` `msgctxt "term|predicate"` keys in `slices/grounding/lang/i18n/{fr,zh}.po` are the authoring seam.

*Note:* the glyph-enrichment branch (PR 1626) is live in these same files and may absorb this.

### 3. The abductive-schema family

The 14 `logic:` abductive-schema terms (`logic:AbductiveSchema`, `logic:AbductiveRepairStrategy`, the four `logic:Strategy*` individuals, `logic:repairsDiscipline`, `logic:repairStrategy`, `logic:completenessFormula`, and the five `*AbductiveSchema` instances) carry a full `rdfs:label` + `skos:definition` and complete fr/zh translations, but raised the coverage ratchet baseline by **+5 on each of nine facets**: `missing-example`, `missing-fixture-pair`, `missing-worked-instance`, `missing-usage-advice`, `missing-scope-note`, `missing-competency-rationale`, `missing-annotation-coat`, `missing-prose-quality`, `missing-test-reach`.

The vocabulary is fully functional and demonstrated (the abductive wing fires on the real `gmeow validate` CLI over an under-specified A-Box) — the shortfall is documentation completeness, not capability.

### 4. The projection-ratchet registry

Adding the registry (2 new `gmeow:` properties + ~154 vocab/ceiling individuals) raised `docs/missing-annotation-coat` by +1 and `docs/missing-competency-rationale` by +15. Recorded at the time as "the annotation debt on the new terms is owed and should be burned down".

## Work

Per family, author the missing dimensions in the term's own home. For the abductive family specifically: `gmeow:example` / worked-instance fixtures, usage advice, scope notes, and competency rationale.

**Do not chase the ratchet number.** Every axis here is an objective intrinsic measure; the goal is real documentation of real terms, and the baseline burning down is the consequence, not the target.

## Acceptance

- The math slice's translation and information coverage rise on measured content, and its floors ratchet up behind them.
- The GMN symbology terms carry fr + cmn.
- The nine facets the abductive family regressed are covered for those 14 terms.

Drained from the local `.deficiencies` ledger (recorded 2026-07-12 and under PR 1580). Re-verified against current `main`. Two publishing/CI paths that have never actually executed.

## A. The PyPI publish leg is validated by construction only

`.github/workflows/pypi-publish-gmeow.yml` exists, the wheel packaging is asserted, and the wheel version is derived deterministically from the ontology's `owl:versionInfo` (PEP 440-validated, stamped into `packages/python/gmeow_models/__about__.py` and read by `[tool.hatch.version]`).

But **no real publish has ever run**: OIDC trusted-publishing needs a live `gmeow-ontology-v*` tag plus the `pypi-gmeow` environment, neither of which a PR can exercise. The path is unexercised end to end, so the first real release is also the first test.

**Work.** Exercise it — a TestPyPI dry run, a dry-run job on the workflow, or a deliberate pre-release tag — so the first real publish is not the first execution.

## B. The check-receipt reuse bootstrap has never engaged

The receipt-backed impact-selection **reuse** fast path (the source of the local `make check` speedup) cannot execute until a successful main-push CI run publishes the attested `gmeow-check-receipt-<base>` artifact. That was an inherent attestation chicken-and-egg at merge time and was accepted as a post-merge bootstrap.

The in-branch mitigation that shipped is real: the reuse **decision** is exercised by tests — a receipt round-trip through the on-disk format validates and authorises a strict-subset selection, and seven tamper cases (wrong registry / toolchain / task-set / status / commit / tree) each fail closed.

What has still never executed is the seam either side of that decision: `obtain_receipt` (CI-artifact download via `gh`) and `verify_attestation` (`gh attestation verify`). Both are network/CI-only.

The recorded post-land obligation was: **on the first main-branch `make check` after the merge, confirm it prints `REUSE` / "verified base receipt ..." rather than silently full-falling-back forever.** That confirmation was never reported. A latent bug in the download/verify seam is invisible to CI and to every PR — `make check` would simply run the full profile forever, which is fail-closed and correct but silently discards the whole feature.

**Work.** Run a main-branch `make check` and record whether it takes the reuse path. If it does not, find out why.

Blocked by: #1642 — which owns the adjacent question of whether the ratchet should net a relocation across its source and destination cells.

## Problem

The projection-vocabulary ratchet works and is green, but it guards a narrower surface than "no hand-authored construct belongs to a generated formalism" implies, and its most useful view is not shippable.

### 1. The counted structural set excludes property signatures, and OWL entirely

`countKindStructuralAxiom` for `rdfs:` counts only `rdfs:subClassOf` and `rdfs:subPropertyOf` — the subsumption taxonomy (`slices/core/slice-quality-rubric/module.ttl:569`). `rdfs:domain` / `rdfs:range` are not counted. The original narrowing was principled: counting property signatures made the projection-vocab schema's own new domain/range declarations net-new debt that the grandfather gate correctly refused to grandfather — a self-referential bootstrap. Narrowing to the subsumption taxonomy resolved it, and RBox declarations are arguably not migration debt.

Separately, declarative OWL is not guarded at all (a deliberate call at the time — "definitely no OWL"), left to the `reason-verify` gate.

Worth revisiting now the bootstrap is past: are domain/range and declarative OWL genuinely out of scope, or were they excluded to get the ratchet landed?

### 2. The grandfathered seed is large and includes cross-slice debt

The strict owner-boundary plus rdfs plus SHACL-obligation counting produced **124 grandfathered ceiling cells** (against 33 under the narrower design), including cross-slice external-reference debt such as correspondence cells sitting in non-owner core slices. This is intended debt, seeded at measured and lower-only — migration ratchets it down. But nothing tracks the burn-down, and cells that are structurally in the wrong slice will never burn down by authoring; they need re-homing.

### 3. The live-measured view is not shippable

`gmeow-dev slice-quality-projection-debt` (`crates/gmeow-dev-cli/src/dev_slice_quality.rs:1588`) is the live migration dashboard — measured residue, headroom, what to migrate next — and it needs a repo checkout to scan. The shippable consumer surface `gmeow slice projection-ceilings` (`crates/gmeow-cli/src/commands.rs:4967`) exposes the **commitments** view only: the registry plus the committed ceilings read from the bundle. A downstream consumer can see what was promised but not how close anything is to breaching.

## Work

- [ ] Decide whether `rdfs:domain`/`range` join the counted set now the bootstrap is resolved.
- [ ] Decide whether declarative OWL gets its own count kind or stays with `reason-verify`.
- [ ] Triage the 124 seeded cells: which burn down by grounding, which need re-homing, which are permanent.
- [ ] Give the shippable surface a measured/headroom view, or state why measurement must stay repo-anchored.

Drained from the local `.deficiencies` ledger (recorded under #1428 and #1609, both closed). Re-verified against current `main`.

## A. The reasoner has two forward mechanisms, not one

`crates/logic/src/reason/math_gate.rs` runs its **own** literal-preserving forward semi-naive chase over a scratch world instead of threading through `reason_program`. The file states why (`math_gate.rs:14-31`): `crate::reason::build_edb_facts` is lossy for this purpose — it drops default-graph quads, and for `reason_program` it drops literal-object quads from the typed EDB fact set. The math dimensional-homogeneity gate needs both: verify's own inputs are default-graph Turtle, and the exact-rational exponent cells are literal facts.

Observable semantics are equivalent today (the gate's input is the full reasoned closure, and the math homogeneity rules do not feed back into the DL strata, so sequential-after-closure equals co-fixpoint for this rule set). The residual is a doctrine trade-off: Principle 19 wants one committed forward path, and there are two.

**Forward path.** Make `build_edb_facts` full-fidelity under an explicit profile — preserving default-graph and literal-object quads — so the math gate, and any future builtin-bound `logic:Constraint` gate, threads through the single `reason_program` path instead of a private chase.

## B. The moded-builtin family has no shipped on-gate driver

The exact-rational arithmetic, SI-dimension 7-vector, and bilinear-form-distance (`bilinearSqDist`) moded builtins are evaluable from all three real reasoner engines (forward `materialize_native`, backward `resolve_native`, reference `reference_resolver`) and are covered by a frozen oracle-gold conformance corpus driven through the public `dispatch_query` surface. That was accepted as sufficient reachability at the time.

But **no shipped on-gate artifact invokes the family**:

- the shipped reasoner profile (`PositiveHornProfile`) rejects builtins outright;
- no shipped `logic:ReasoningProgram` queries a builtin;
- `gmeow affect nearest` computes its squared distance via `gmeow_math::InnerProductSpace` directly, bypassing `bilinearSqDist`.

So `make check` never exercises an exact-rational / dimension / bilinear builtin query on a production surface.

**Forward path.** Expose a production surface that drives the procedural-profile shared evaluator on-gate — a `gmeow` CLI subcommand over `dispatch_query` under `ProceduralPrologProfile`, and/or a shipped `logic:ReasoningProgram` that the `reason-verify` gate runs.

## Acceptance

- The math dimensional-homogeneity gate produces its findings through `reason_program`, and the private chase is deleted (greenfield: no second mechanism left behind).
- A `make check` run exercises at least one moded builtin on a shipped surface.

Drained from the local `.deficiencies` ledger (recorded across #1295, #1344, #1413). Each of those issues is closed; these residues were recorded with explicit forward paths and never tracked.

## Five residues in the native reasoner

### A. Large-cardinality cases withhold rather than decide

The DL-consistency reasoner enforces hard existential-chase materialization backstops: a per-obligation witness ceiling of 512, a 500,000-fact chase bound, and a 20,000-step backstop. A case whose existential / number-cardinality materialization would exceed a bound folds into an honest `reason.dl-gap.chase-materialization-bound` withhold.

This is sound — a withhold is never a wrong answer, so `corpus_only` stays 0 — and it replaced a genuinely worse behaviour (a `>=n` cardinality lowered to n witnesses plus n*(n-1)/2 pairwise `owl:differentFrom` atoms; at n=60000 that is ~1.8 billion atoms and an unbounded ~50 GB allocation). But it is a weaker mechanism than a complete cardinality decision procedure: the W3C suite's `webont-i5-1-010` (`owl:cardinality 127`) and `webont-description-logic-905/906/907` (up to 60000) now withhold.

**Forward path.** A non-materializing / symbolic cardinality decision procedure that reasons over `>=n` and pairwise-distinctness constraints structurally, without generating n witnesses and n^2 differentFrom atoms.

### B. The super-weak-acyclicity certifier is conservative

The shipped SWA certifier is a sound but conservative rendering of Marnette's super-weak acyclicity — a static Skolemized place graph with **one-hop** unification. It never over-certifies and is non-vacuous beyond weak acyclicity, but where a null is laundered through an intermediate datalog rule it conservatively refuses, so some genuinely super-weakly-acyclic programs fall through to Uncertified (and thence to budget) rather than being certified.

**Forward path.** Full multi-hop unification-reachability, tracking the Skolem term through datalog laundering. This converges toward the MSA/MFA critical-instance machinery already shipped for the MSA rung.

### C. Guardedness and stickiness need a different paradigm — and must not be faked

The chase-termination ladder certifies joint, super-weak, and model-summarizing acyclicity. Guardedness and stickiness are **not** chase-termination certificates: a guarded or sticky TGD program can still have an infinite chase.

**This is a correctness warning, not just a gap.** They must NOT be added as `ChaseAdmission` rungs routed through `admits_native` — admitting such a program to the native terminating chase would be unsound. Supporting them requires a separate evaluation strategy decided on its own surface: a bounded-treewidth chase for guardedness, FO-rewriting / backward chase for stickiness.

### D. SLG-WFS is batch, not incremental

Well-founded negation is built (van-Gelder alternating fixpoint), but incremental well-founded maintenance remains the longest-standing perf gap, flagged non-incremental in the perf ledger and in `LOGIC-RUNTIME.md`'s staging.

### E. Five W3C OWL2-Full cases are unparsable, so they grade as pure SKIPs

The native RDF/XML ingestion path cannot read premises that embed a `<!DOCTYPE ... <!ENTITY ...>>` DTD (the hardened parser refuses DTDs as XXE mitigation) or an `rdf:datatype` node element. Affected: `consistent-but-all-unsat`, `webont-miscellaneous-001`, `webont-miscellaneous-002`, `webont-oneof-004`, `fs2rdf-literals-ar`.

The grader correctly treats these as SKIPs rather than spurious reasoner gaps (a malformed/unparsable source is a corpus defect, not a capability gap), so `make maint-external-corpora` exits clean with `corpus_only=0` — but the five cases are simply not graded.

**Forward path.** Route DTD-bearing premises through the existing `expand_xml_entities` helper (or a safe entity-expansion pass) before parsing, and support `rdf:datatype` node elements, so the five ingest and can be graded.

## Work

Each of A-E is independently landable. C is a design decision first (do we want either paradigm?), and its only mandatory outcome is that nobody adds them as acyclicity rungs.

Drained from the local `.deficiencies` ledger (recorded 2026-07-12 and 2026-07-17). Re-verified against current `main`.

## Problem

Cutting the schema emitters over to purrdf's `CompiledSchema` basis unified the derive-source (good, and intended) but dropped a set of shipped developer-surface capabilities that were never re-homed. Recorded at the time as a user-approved capability regression; nothing tracks recovering it.

### Pydantic: a flat module with no ontology linkage

`packages/python/gmeow_models/` is now `__about__.py`, `__init__.py`, `_base.py`, `models.py` (2.6 MB), `py.typed`. Verified on the shipped package:

- `grep -c definitionDigest packages/python/gmeow_models/models.py` -> **0**
- `grep -c json_schema_extra packages/python/gmeow_models/models.py` -> **0**

So the following are gone, not re-homed (`crates/pipeline/src/stages/pydantic.rs:19-35` documents each):

- **Per-slice modules.** Each class used to route into its owning slice's module (`gmeow_models/<slice>.py`, ~40 modules) so a slice's models were independently importable, with the slice's tier/DOI header in the module docstring. Everything is now one flat `models.py`.
- **Docs-digest linkage.** `json_schema_extra` carried the term's `gmeow:definitionDigest`, and the class docstring carried definition / when-to-use / avoid / how-to-use, worked examples, a runnable usage doctest, and a docs back-link URL. A model class now carries only its compiled-schema identity — no term-prose linkage at all.
- **Generated package `README.md`.**

Upstream feature request: `Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf` issue 130 (per-slice module routing, per-class docs/definition-digest linkage, caller-supplied version stamping).

### Developer schemas now cover exactly the SHACL shape union

LinkML / TypeScript / GraphQL moved from a hand-rolled OWL to LinkML projection onto the SHACL-derived basis. Consequence: OWL-only / RBox properties with no derived SHACL property shape are no longer in these surfaces. Concretely `gmeow:resentDate` and `gmeow:resentMessageId` (email slice, `gmeow:graphBoxRole gmeow:boxRBox`, non-functional DatatypeProperties) are absent from `generated/schemas/gmeow.linkml.yaml`, `gmeow.schema.json`, and `models.py`. They remain canonical in the OWL/RDF layer, enforced by the slice's structural assertion — but a developer reading the schemas cannot see them. Upstream: purrdf issue 134.

### Two further accepted format changes

- JSON-LD serialization emits an empty `@context` (examples/goldens now carry full IRIs). Upstream: purrdf issue 135.
- `gmeow export` CSVW is purrdf's generic lossless RDF-1.2-in-CSV carrier (large), replacing the retired curated class/property/individual term-dictionary tables. Upstream: purrdf issue 136.

### There is now no live-Python conformance at all

The ledger recorded that live-Python conformance was off the merge-blocking gate, running only in `make maint-pydantic-conformance`. Both are now gone: no `maint-pydantic-conformance` target exists in the Makefile, and `packages/python/tests/` does not exist (`test_conformance.py` was deleted as asserting a layout that no longer exists). The only remaining check is the Rust structural agreement gate `emitted_models_agree_with_packed_schema_defs` — which proves the emitted `.py` agrees with the compiled `$defs` but never runs a Python interpreter. A package that structurally agrees yet fails to import passes every gate in the repo.

## Work

- [ ] Decide per capability: recover in-repo, wait on the upstream issue, or ratify the loss in `docs/schema-projections.md`.
- [ ] Restore some form of term-to-model linkage (`definitionDigest` and a docs back-link are the minimum that makes the wheel navigable).
- [ ] Re-establish a live import + `model_json_schema()` agreement check somewhere — off-gate is fine, absent is not.
- [ ] Decide whether OWL-only/RBox properties should be surfaced in the developer schemas or documented as deliberately out of scope.

## Acceptance

- A consumer of the wheel can get from a model class back to its ontology term.
- The generated package is proven to import, in some lane.

| Excluded | What it proves |

| `gmeow-pipeline & binary(fold_parity)` | the sink fold matches the committed per-named-graph bundle (`sink_fold_matches_committed_per_named_graph`) |
| `gmeow-validate & binary(conformance_math_producers)` | the math producers' SHACL conformance (15/15) |
| `gmeow-conformance & binary(full_divergence_gate) & /_heavy_offgate/` | the 154-case soundness scaling proof (`never_a_wrong_decided_verdict_heavy_offgate`, `native_reproduces_the_frozen_gap_heavy_offgate`) |

| `gmeow-docs & binary(mdbook_render)` (5 tests) | the emitted mdbook source tree |

**Sharper finding — one audit runs in no lane at all.** `every_real_slice_batch_matches_parallel_scratch` (the exhaustive all-slice batch-vs-scratch reasoner parity audit) is excluded by a Rust attribute, not the filter: `crates/slice-quality/src/reasoner.rs:741` carries `#[ignore = "exhaustive repo audit; ..."]`. `[profile.maint-heavy]` sets `default-filter = 'all()'` (`.config/nextest.toml:59`), but `all()` does **not** un-`#[ignore]` a test. **Related fragility.** `ACCEPTANCE_MIN_RECALL_PCT = 64.5` (`crates/pipeline/src/scoreboards.rs:766`) sits against a measured corpus-aggregate round-trip recall of 64.57 % — 0.07 pp of headroom, so ordinary corpus drift reds the gate.

## Work

This is a repo-wide gate-placement decision, not a per-PR one. For each excluded lane, choose exactly one and record the choice where the exclusion lives:

- [ ] **Promote on-gate** — if it can be made to fit the budget.
- [ ] **Move to `maint-heavy`** — and for `#[ignore]`d tests, actually make `maint-heavy` run them (an `#[ignore]` is invisible to `default-filter = 'all()'`; it needs `run-ignored = "all"` or the attribute removed under that profile).
- [ ] **Ratify the on-gate proxy in writing** — name the proxy and what it does not cover, next to the exclusion.

- [ ] Decide whether `every_real_slice_batch_matches_parallel_scratch` should run anywhere; today it does not.
- [ ] Re-baseline or widen the headroom on `ACCEPTANCE_MIN_RECALL_PCT`, or document the 0.07 pp margin as intended.

## Acceptance

- Every entry in the `default-filter` exclusion list carries an inline justification naming its on-gate proxy or its off-gate home.
- No test is excluded from every lane.

body:
## Consumer

Project Lillith needs **durable work clusters**: continuing goals with
versioned plans, guidance, notes, recurring fresh runs, resumable progress,
contextual recommendations, and safe execution of externally effectful
actions. A weekly "review and comment on ADRs" cluster must revisit the same
maintenance goal as the ADR corpus changes, retain what was learned, create a
new immutable run each week, and show the operator a comprehensive current
frontier. An abstract step such as "OCR PDF" should be refined into executable
preparation and verification work when an approved capability exists, or into
a complete operational capability-gap proposal when it does not.

This is a Principle 15 consumer request. It builds on the canonical process
model from #1054/#1055 rather than creating another workflow ontology.

## Pre-flight and existing semantic base

The current vocabulary already supplies much of the semantic substrate and it
MUST be reused:

- `logic:Plan`, `logic:ActionSchema`, goal expressions/evaluations,
  preconditions, effects, invariants, resources, capabilities, observations,
  nondeterministic outcomes, and per-outcome compensation from #1055;
- `gmeow:Procedure`, `gmeow:ProcedureStep`, control/data flow, and execution as
  projection surfaces;
- `gmeow:EventSeries` and `gmeow:RecurrenceRule` for recurrence;
- goal refinement and AND/OR decomposition (`gmeow:refinesGoal`,
  necessary/sufficient/contributing structure);
- `gmeow:Note`, annotations, comments, provenance, standpoint, temporal,
  lifecycle, and content-digest vocabulary;
- the preference extension's `gmeow:CandidateSet`,
  `gmeow:ComparisonContext`, attributed observations/evaluations,
  criteria/rubrics, contextual partial orders, hard-failure handling, and
  consensus-gated projections.

A search of current issues found no open issue covering the combined
durable-run, active-refinement, and external-effect contract. #1055 is the
semantic base, but does not provide the operational identity, checkpoint,
reconciliation, idempotency, or active-assistance vocabulary requested here.
Existing `gmeow:CapabilityGap` is reasoner/profile-conformance terminology; it
must not be overloaded for an absent operational tool/provider.

## Required semantic contract

Please design the **maximal coherent vocabulary/profile**, reusing existing
terms wherever their identity criteria fit. Candidate names below describe
required concepts, not a demand to duplicate or pre-assign slice ownership.

### 1. Continuing work identity and immutable versions

Represent, and keep distinct:

- a continuing `WorkCluster` that binds a maintenance/achievement goal,
  governing policy, recurrence, active plan version, guidance set, note set,
  and history;
- an immutable `WorkPlanVersion` whose canonical plan is a `logic:Plan`,
  content-addressed and explicitly superseded rather than mutated;
- an immutable `WorkRun`/`PlanExecution` against exactly one plan version and
  one closed input/generation snapshot;
- durable run and step checkpoints, with version/digest bindings sufficient
  to reject a mismatched restore;
- `resume` as continuation of the same run, `repeat` as a new run under a new
  input snapshot, and `revise` as a new plan/guidance version;
- lifecycle axes that do not conflate run state, step state, approval state,
  effect state, goal-evaluation state, and recurrence state.

A successful occurrence of a recurring maintenance plan MUST NOT imply that
the continuing maintenance goal is permanently satisfied.

### 2. Active plan refinement and preparation

Represent an attributed, bounded `PlanRefinementEpisode` that takes an
abstract/unexecutable plan step plus the current world/policy/capability
snapshot and produces:

- a closed candidate set of subplans/action schemas;
- explicit refinement/decomposition links back to the abstract step and
  served goal;
- precondition/capability/resource/approval checks and rejection reasons per
  candidate;
- preparation activities and `PreparationReceipt`s for work completed before
  the selected action becomes ready;
- an immutable selected/pinned executable subgraph when a candidate is
  authorized;
- or an `OperationalCapabilityGap` plus `CapabilityGapProposal` naming the
  missing capability, required contract, expected inputs/outputs/effects,
  verification method, security/lifecycle needs, and the blocked step.

A model-generated decomposition, recommendation, summary, or draft is
attributed advice/evidence. It is never semantic authority, never silently
changes the plan, and never licenses an effect by itself.

### 3. Closed actionable frontier and decision support

Represent the derived, closed next-action frontier of a run. It must
distinguish at least:

- ready and policy-authorized;
- ready but approval-required;
- blocked by unmet precondition;
- blocked by missing capability/resource;
- waiting for event/time/input;
- mutually exclusive with another candidate;
- reconciliation-required after an uncertain effect;
- compensation-eligible or compensation-required;
- completed, skipped with a typed reason, cancelled, and terminally failed.

Map candidate actions/subplans into the existing preference apparatus rather
than minting a second recommendation model. Recommendations are relative to a
`ComparisonContext` and may be a partial order with ties or incomparability.
No context-free or unjustified global winner is permitted. The operator
projection should be able to explain every recommended/blocked action with
proof, evidence, policy, cost/risk/benefit criteria, and dissenting attributed
observations.

### 4. Durable external-effect saga vocabulary

Add the operational records needed around `logic:ActionSchema` and transaction
paths:

- a pre-effect `DispatchIntent` bound to run, step/attempt, action
  schema/version, exact normalized arguments, target/resource, policy,
  approval requirement, and content digest;
- an `EffectAttempt` and provider correlation identity;
- an `ExternalEffectReceipt` describing observed outcome and evidence;
- an `ExternalOutcomeUnknown` state for the crash/timeout boundary where
  dispatch may have occurred but no authoritative outcome is known;
- an `IdempotencyContract` with scope, key, expiry/retention, duplicate
  semantics, and provider support evidence;
- a `ReconciliationProbe`/`ReconciliationAttempt` and result that can
  establish committed/not-committed/still-unknown before retry or compensation;
- compensation eligibility, `CompensationAttempt`, and compensation outcome,
  linked to the exact forward effect/outcome it addresses;
- semantic resource claims/leases or locks with ownership, scope, fencing
  identity, and expiry where concurrency requires them;
- budget/cost/deadline consumption and exhaustion records;
- an `ApprovalGrant` bound to the exact dispatch-intent digest, run/step,
  authorized operator identity, policy, decision, and validity window.

Compensation is a new action with its own preconditions, effects, attempts,
receipts, and possible failure; it is not erasure and must not be modeled as
guaranteed inverse "undo." The ontology/logic engine describes, validates,
derives, and certifies these records. A consumer-owned Rust organ performs
persistence and physical dispatch; GMEOW MUST NOT be described as committing
external effects.

### 5. Guidance, working memory, and review projection

Represent versioned guidance/rubrics/checklists, retained notes and
observations, which notes were surfaced to a run, which guidance version
governed it, and provenance for model/operator/tool contributions. Support a
comprehensive projection containing:

- continuing goal and recurrence;
- current plan and revision lineage;
- current run and exact input snapshot;
- derived todo/frontier with recommendations and blockers;
- approvals and pending inputs;
- effect/reconciliation/compensation status;
- accumulated notes, decisions, artifacts, receipts, and prior-run comparison;
- an exact accessible graph/timeline representation and a presentation
  projection receipt.

## Required native reasoning surface

Principles 12 and 17 require the means-end and operational checks to be
solver-side over canonical `logic:` semantics. Provide bounded, typed
query/derivation contracts that can:

1. derive the closed actionable frontier for a run;
2. search from an abstract step to candidate executable subplans using
   available action schemas and declared capabilities;
3. return proof/rejection witnesses, completeness status, and exhausted
   resource/budget information;
4. validate the selected refinement and pin its executable subgraph;
5. classify whether an effect may dispatch, requires approval, is blocked, or
   requires reconciliation;
6. forbid blind retry after `ExternalOutcomeUnknown` unless the declared
   idempotency/reconciliation contract makes it safe;
7. derive compensation eligibility/requirements without asserting that
   compensation succeeded;
8. compare candidate actions contextually through the existing preference
   vocabulary, preserving ties and incomparability;
9. distinguish operational incompleteness/capability absence from a
   reasoning-profile `gmeow:CapabilityGap`.

The result must distinguish complete derivation, incomplete-by-budget or
cancellation, unsupported fragment, invalid input, and engine failure. No
heuristic/model answer may be relabeled as a proof.

## Competency and negative cases

### Weekly ADR review

A continuing maintenance cluster repeats weekly. Each occurrence creates a
fresh immutable run against a closed ADR-corpus generation, surfaces applicable
guidance and retained notes, discovers newly added/changed ADRs, derives review
actions, and records comments/drafts/decisions as attributed artifacts.
Resuming a paused occurrence continues that run; next week creates another. One
successful week does not close the maintenance goal.

### Abstract "OCR PDF" step

Given an abstract step and a PDF:

- when a governed OCR action schema/capability exists, refinement produces a
  pinned subplan such as inspect -> prepare -> OCR -> verify -> store receipt,
  and policy-maximal automation may execute all authorized non-approval
  effects;
- when it does not exist, the frontier contains a blocked action plus a
  complete `CapabilityGapProposal`; no invented tool call, weaker fallback, or
  false completion is permitted.

### Crash at the effect boundary

Persisted dispatch intent exists, the provider may have accepted the action,
and no receipt was durably recorded. The run enters `ExternalOutcomeUnknown`;
a restart derives reconciliation as the next action and cannot blindly
redispatch or compensate.

### Exact approval binding

Approval for one digest/target/argument set cannot authorize a revised intent,
different run, expired request, or different operator-policy binding.

### Contextual recommendation

Two valid next actions are ordered under one policy/standpoint, tied under
another, and incomparable under a third. The graph preserves all attributed
evaluations and never fabricates a universal winner.

### Required negatives

- checkpoint restored against a different plan/input/action-schema digest;
- `resume`, `repeat`, and `revise` conflated;
- mutable plan history overwritten in place;
- effect receipt asserted without an attempt/intent;
- unknown outcome treated as ordinary failure and retried;
- compensation treated as guaranteed inverse or marked successful without a
  receipt;
- approval detached from the exact effect intent;
- a model recommendation asserted as proof or authorization;
- incomplete candidate/frontier roster presented as closed;
- absent OCR capability silently replaced by a weaker parser.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Design charter with identity criteria, lifecycle axes, state-transition
  laws, reuse ledger, and explicit non-conflation rules.
- [ ] Canonical RDF 1.2 / `logic:` vocabulary plus required core/extension
  ownership and projection-loss decisions.
- [ ] Native logic query/derivation contracts for refinement, frontier,
  dispatch gating, reconciliation, and compensation eligibility.
- [ ] Structural, competency, counterexample, crash/replay, and digest-mismatch
  conformance fixtures.
- [ ] Mappings/projections for relevant PROV-O/P-Plan/BPMN/Temporal-style
  concepts only where preservation is explicit; no external workflow system
  becomes semantic authority.
- [ ] Consumer examples for weekly ADR review and OCR
  capability-present/capability-absent paths.
- [ ] Generated documentation and `make check` green.

## Constitutional alignment

- **Principles 2/3:** RDF 1.2-native provenance and statement metadata.
- **Principles 4/5:** extend the one canonical `logic:Plan`/action/preference
  model and reuse existing terms before minting.
- **Principle 9:** contextual recommendations preserve standpoint plurality
  and do not create a privileged winner.
- **Principle 12:** bounded means-end search and derivation live in the native
  logic engine; the ontology records the contract.
- **Principle 15:** Lillith is the named consumer with concrete weekly-review
  and OCR scenarios.
- **Principles 17/18:** canonical `logic:` semantics, native Rust reasoning,
  offline-capable and fail-closed; projections are governed loss surfaces.

> **Tracking epic.** This issue coordinates the slice-authoring-factory work; it carries no code of its own and closes only when every sub-issue below has closed. Per `AGENTS.md § 5` (Work Sizing), an epic that no single PR can close is decomposed into blocking/dependent sub-issues — this is decomposition, not deferral: every requirement below lives in exactly one tracked child.

## Problem

Per-slice annotation coats and translations collapse into gamed boilerplate when attempted as monolithic PRs — the evidence is the closed grounding/math full-uplift PR (#1498): 1,184-entry templated catalogs, boilerplate `useWhen`/`avoidWhen` coats, class-projected named-individual mappings. The honest surface remaining on math alone is ~691 uncoated terms and ~1,383 untranslated literals × fr/zh, and every slice in the repo carries the same obligation. Downstream slice authors face it with even less infrastructure: `principia` (10 tierCore slices, ~635 labels, 212 definitions) authors plain hand-edited Turtle with **zero local tooling**, consuming gmeow by path+commit pin.

The quality machinery (measured axes, integrity guards, raise-only floors) already prevents regression. What is missing is the machinery that makes **genuine authoring cheap**: self-contained work packets, an honest intermediate state for translations, and a gate that kills the next template family before mass authoring begins.

## The concept: the semantic packet, formalized

`docs/SLICE-UPGRADE.md` already defines the unit of curation as a **semantic packet**. This epic formalizes it as a typed, machine-readable authoring obligation — `gmeow:AuthoringPacket` — derived deterministically from measured axis findings, enriched with all the context an author needs, consumable by humans, agents, and (eventually) self-authoring systems, and verified by deterministic gates.

**Propose–verify neurosymbolic architecture:** the symbolic side (axes, gates, oracles) emits obligations and verifies candidates; the neural side (human/LLM) generates. Generation is untrusted; verification is trusted; a score can ONLY move via gate-passing content in canonical slice sources. This is the seam through which future self-authoring systems plug into the pipeline.

## Workstreams (tracking)

Seven completable sub-issues, each a single landable PR behind the ratcheted floor. Foundation A is split into a pure-refactor A1 and the new-surface A2 to isolate landing risk.

- [ ] **#1531 — A1** de-wire the slice-quality engine + make it wheel-shippable *(pure refactor; foundation)*
- [ ] **#1532 — A2** `gmeow slice quality/lint` consumer subcommands
- [ ] **#1533 — B** `gmeow:AuthoringPacket` type + brief projection + `gmeow slice brief`
- [ ] **#1534 — C** fuzzy-gated translation coverage
- [ ] **#1535 — D** distinctiveness / near-duplicate guard
- [ ] **#1536 — E** MCP surface: consumer `slice_quality`, `slice_brief`, candidate submission
- [ ] **#1537 — F** batch contract + fr/zh glossary lint

### Dependency DAG

```
A1 (#1531) ──▶ A2 (#1532) ──▶ B (#1533) ──▶ E (#1536)
     └──────────────────────────────────────▶ E (#1536)
C (#1534) ─┐
D (#1535) ─┼──▶ F (#1537)
B (#1533) ─┘
```

Edges: #1531 ▶ {#1532, #1536}; #1532 ▶ #1533; #1533 ▶ {#1536, #1537}; #1534 ▶ #1537; #1535 ▶ #1537. #1536 and #1537 are leaves. Buildable-now front: **#1531, #1534, #1535** (nothing blocks them).

### Two corrections verified against the code (folded into the children)

- **No path-escape guard exists** to lift (A1): `dev_slice_quality.rs` does no `canonicalize`/`starts_with(root)`/`..` rejection — arbitrary dirs are already accepted. The real blockers are the repo-path-wired rubric, the wheel-only razor, and the two repo-anchored axes (`gmn1_coverage`, `DocMaturity`).
- **`gmeow:TermEquivalence` carries no fr/zh labels** (B): its only label fields are optional *English* `subjectLabel`/`objectLabel`; translations live in per-slice `.po` catalogs. The brief must **join** TermEquivalence cells with the `.po` index, not pull fr/zh from the cells.

## Non-goals

- No LLM calls inside the deterministic pipeline (drafting happens out-of-pipeline via CLI/MCP consumers).
- No auto-derived floors (NO-CALIBRATION — the seeder stays emit-only, commitment stays a human decision).
- No coats authored by template.

# EPIC — Closed-world constraint canonicalization: blanket shape-purity seal, zero legacy

Canonicalize the entire closed-world constraint corpus so every SHACL/ShEx shape is a
projection of slice constraint axioms, land a **blanket** shape-purity seal, and delete the
whole hand-authored shape corpus + the structural `write_shex` export. Single source of truth.

Driven by `.goals`/`.baseline` (no deferrals, no compromises, no optionality, keep no legacy):
the gate is blanket, and a blanket gate is green only when the corpus is clean — so the migration
is executed to completion, not softened to a "detector".

## Foundation (landed on `paudley/1193-shape-subsumption-blanket-seal`)
- Subsumption engine (`≡`/`⊑` over the `ConstraintComponent` lattice).
- Equivalence oracle + comparison-only SHACL→IR reader + non-vacuous cross-check.
- Lift = the projector's Galois adjoint, certified against the real forward derive.
- Blanket declarative purity gate (proven over the live corpus; activates at the terminal increment).
- Typed `Shacl`/`Shex` lookaside sidecars into `gmeow.gts`.
- `conformance/validation/` projection-correctness category.
- `gmeow-dev shape-equivalence` — the per-increment verifier and the **live coverage ledger**
  (exits non-zero until every authored shape is grounded; this is the epic done-condition, no
  staleable committed snapshot).
- Proving slices `inference` + `inhabitation` grounded end-to-end (14 classes), oracle-verified.

## Remaining increments (per-slice; each: lift → author axioms in the owning slice → oracle `EQUIV` → delete legacy block)
~160 legacy shapes remain, by owning slice:
- `slices/extensions/music` (~33)
- `shapes/gmeow-shapes.ttl` — re-home ~78 to owning slices
- `slices/core/epistemics` (~8), `slices/core/ai` (~5)
- `shapes/mapping-dsl-shapes.ttl` (~12), `shapes/test-dsl-shapes.ttl`
- `slices/extensions/{model-serving,graphrag,agentic}`, `slices/core/{temporal,gts,standpoint,pipeline,notation,kernel,concepts,learning,diagnostics}`
- tail singletons

Run `gmeow-dev shape-equivalence --path <slice>` to see a slice's current verdicts.

## Residue-bearing classes (no faithful shape projection — carried in the canon, ledgered)
Some legacy shapes carry `sh:or` type-disjunction, value-keyed `sh:SPARQLTarget`, or nested
`sh:node` conditions the dataset-derive cannot reproduce (e.g. `AttackShape`, `SupportShape`,
`AbductionCommitmentShape`, `InhabitationTenureShape`). These are grounded either by extending the
derive or by authoring the condition as a full-FOL `logic:` constraint (projecting to the SHACL
constraint surface) — never deleted with their check dropped.

## Terminal increment
When the ledger reaches 0: wire the blanket gate active into `check_repo_static`; delete all
remaining hand-authored `**/shapes.ttl` + the structural `write_shex`/`dist/gmeow.shex`; repoint
consumers to the generated surface. This is where #1193 closes (`Closes #1193, #1194`) — its
headline gate reaches production with `make check` green.

body:
## Thesis

GMEOW needs **two compressed forms, never conflated**, organized on **two orthogonal axes**:

```text
dialect axis (semantic):   GMN-0 normal form → GMN-1 token-compact → GMN-2 compaction
medium axis (physical):    GTS bytes | canonical N-Quads/Turtle | zstd-dict frames | JSON-LD …
```

1. **Machine compression (medium axis)** — GTS binary + per-corpus trained zstd dictionaries for storage, packets, cache, and transport. An invisible byte layer. **Never model-facing: do not train or prompt an LLM on compressed bytes** — it wastes model capacity learning compression noise.
2. **Model compression (dialect axis)** — **GMN, the GMEOW Model Notation**: a token-efficient, canonical, readable textual dialect that LLMs read and write for training, prompting, repair, and generation. Inspired by the schema-once/columnar tricks of TOON/JTON/ONTO, but GMEOW-native — generic compact notations do not know what must be abbreviated, preserved, typechecked, ring-filtered, or forbidden to leak.

The razor that keeps the two apart: **physical compression is lossless and identity-preserving — a zstd-compressed claim is the same claim. Cognitive compaction is a NEW claim about older claims.** GMN-2 lives on the dialect axis with an honest `lossy` ledger entry and provenance links; zstd lives on the medium axis and never changes semantics. A dialect is an abstraction level with its own preservation contract; a codec is a medium ("Canadian-English-written-on-paper" is not a dialect).

Symbology is **ontology-native**: if `⊑` is the symbol for a `logic:` term, that is asserted on the term itself in the DSL (via `lang:Denotation` from a Sign in the GMN Script), and the GMN toolchain **derives** its lexicon and grammar from the graph. The notation cannot drift from the semantics because both are minted at the same waist.

The end goal: GMN becomes a **lingua franca for LLMs speaking GMEOW** — compact prompts, stable training examples, constrained-decoding-friendly grammar, proof-grounded repair loops, and an ecosystem surface (primer card, conformance suite, MCP verifier, WASM validator) that lets models we do not control speak it reliably.

## Formal spine

- **GMN-0 = the RDF normal form** — the *existing* narrow-waist canonicalization (RDFC-1.0 canonical blank-node labeling + content-sorted term table in `gts_compose`, per `docs/gts-narrow-waist.md`). GMN-0 is a *name* for something that already exists; it is medium-independent (GTS and canonical N-Quads are correspondence-carrying **encodings** of it). It mints NO rival canonical object and is trivially mnemomorphic.
- **GMN-1 = the token-compact LLM surface** — sigil records, schema-once tabular batches, ontology-derived glyphs/aliases. Well-behaved with ledgered loss; its round-trip gate anchors against the GMN-0 **dataset**, not any file format.
- **GMN-2 = lossy cognitive compaction** — a reified new claim about older claims, provenance-linked, get-leg-only correspondence, honestly `lossy` in the ledger. Sources stay retrievable; compaction never overwrites.
- **Every dialect level and every inter-level/inter-version relation is a `logic:Correspondence`** (get/put legs) with a `logic:preservationKind` judgment (mnemomorphic / well-behaved / lossy — vocabulary verbatim) and a loss-ledger entry, riding the existing `lang:translationCorrespondence` rail (Principle 17 applied to our own notation).
- **GMN is specified, created, and projected THROUGH `lang:`**: GMN-1 is a `lang:SignSystem` (engineered notation; `Language ⊑ SignSystem` holds post-#1271); its glyph inventory is a `lang:Script`; its NFC/confusables/canonical-form norms are a `lang:Orthography`; glyph↔term bindings are `lang:Denotation`s; emission registers as a `LangProjectionTarget` in the PROJECTIONS registry (preservation **derived, not declared**); ingestion of LLM-emitted GMN is a RUNTIME lane.
- **Namespace ruling:** `gmn:` is NOT a top-level namespace. GMN terms live in the main `gmeow:` namespace with `gmn`-prefixed local names (`gmeow:gmnGlyph`, `gmeow:gmnCodepoints`, `gmeow:gmnFixity`).
- **Dialect versions are first-class ontology individuals** — each released version (e.g. GMN-1 v0.7) is a versioned `lang:SignSystem` with a frozen Script + Orthography + alias-table snapshot; the in-band `@gmn` header and packet envelope resolve to that node. Inter-version migration is a correspondence whose preservation judgment makes the semver promise checkable (mnemomorphic iff additive-only; the overclaim gate polices bumps). Greenfield preserved: only the CURRENT version is authored in the canonical core; prior versions persist as frozen generated artifacts + migration correspondences ("lossy compatibility lives only in generated projections").
- **Envelope contract on every compact artifact:** schema version, dictionary version, alias/glyph-table version, security ring, standpoint, provenance, losslessness flag, canonical blake3 hash. Compression never erases semantics.
- **The optimization target is a metric vector, never byte size alone:**

```text
bytes_on_disk · tokens_in_context · AST_validity_rate · roundtrip_loss ·
proof_success_rate · repair_success_rate · generation_latency
```

## Architecture

GMN as lang: individuals + a small graft module (the #1271 grafting pattern):

```text
gmeow:Gmn1SignSystem_v0_1   a lang:SignSystem      # versioned; frozen per release
gmeow:GmnScript_v0_1        a lang:Script          # the glyph inventory (codepoint-explicit)
gmeow:GmnOrthography_v0_1   a lang:Orthography     # NFC, confusables, canonical-form norms
<sign> lang:denotation …    # glyph ↔ ontology-term binding; gmeow:gmnGlyph is a DERIVED convenience
GMN-0→1, 1→2, vN→vN+1       # lang:translationCorrespondence carrying logic:Correspondence
gmeow:gmnFixity / precedence / sigil-role   # only what lang: lacks
```

Sigil grammar (sigils are record-initial ONLY — resolves μ-as-measure vs `@μ` collisions):

```text
claim @c · evidence @e · standpoint @s · process @p · proof @π
defeater @d · modal @m · math @μ · lang_ast @λ · logic @ℒ
```

Record and schema-once tabular batch forms:

```text
@c{id:c9, s:tulpa, p:affectToward, o:project_x, v:curious_guarded,
   q:.71, st:self/current, ev:[e12,e33], mod:affective}

@claims[id s p o v q st ev mod]
c1 tulpa affectToward project_x curious_guarded .71 self/current e12,e33 affective
c2 tulpa trustToward coworker_y moderate .62 self/current e44,e45 social
```

Model-facing loops (both directions, every step a named seam):

```text
retrieve → zstd decode → canonicalize (GMN-0) → privacy/ring filter → GMN-1 → token budget → LLM
LLM emits GMN-1 → Rust parse → glyph/alias expand → typecheck → prover → store canonical → zstd
```

Training corpus = paired examples (NL / packet / proof-failure / retrieved context → target GMN-1), **rejection-sampled by the Rust parser/prover verifier**: parses, roundtrips, typechecks, proof obligation generated, no forbidden ring leakage.

## Lingua-franca design levers

- **LL(1)-ish, prefix-stable, newline-delimited grammar** engineered for constrained decoding; GBNF/Lark/schema forms emitted as **generated projections of the graph** (grammar drift impossible by construction).
- **Key order mirrors generation order** (`s p o v q st ev` — decide-first fields first); fixed number policy (2-digit confidences, no scientific notation — digit tokenization is a minefield).
- **Token-cost matrix across real tokenizer vocabs** (o200k/cl100k/Llama/Qwen/Gemma) as a `maint-` lane artifact over vendored vocab data; the deterministic estimator remains the gate. An ASCII digraph beats a fragmenting Unicode glyph, full stop; prior-alignment only pays if the glyph is cheap.
- **Self-describing**: in-band header `@gmn v<schema> aliases:<table>`; a generated ~500-token **primer card** distributed via llms.txt + MCP.
- **In-dialect repair loop**: verifier failures return as GMN `@err` records; `@patch`/`@retract` delta sub-dialect over stable record IDs; MCP verifier tools (`gmn_validate` / `gmn_expand` / `gmn_explain`) so external LLMs join the loop without local tooling.
- **Determinism as a runtime feature**: byte-identical canonical serialization → prompt-cache hits, KV-prefix reuse, training-data dedup.
- **Stability**: semver'd, additive-only-within-major notation surface (alias tables absorb churn); public conformance suite (W3C-corpora precedent); WASM validator (purrdf-wasm lane); deterministic GMN↔controlled-NL verbalizer as a lang:translationCorrespondence (free bidirectional training pairs).

## Prior art (borrow the tricks, adopt nothing unchanged)

| Scheme | Use |
| --- | --- |
| TOON | token-efficient JSON-ish notation; repeated-record pattern |
| JTON / Zen Grid | "schema once, rows many" for batches |
| ONTO | columnar notation for LLM input; repeated-key elimination |
| Turtle / compacted JSON-LD | interop projections; not token-optimal |
| HDT / binary RDF | storage/indexing ideas; bad direct LLM surface |
| zstd dictionaries | transport/storage layer only; never model-facing |

Refs: KL3M domain tokenizers (arXiv:2503.17247); ONTO (arXiv:2604.17512); JTON (arXiv:2604.05865).

## What is preserved

- The narrow waist: GMN-0 IS the existing normal form; every GMN artifact and every `.zdict` is a projection of `gmeow.gts` (PIPELINE_SPINE doctrine).
- The correspondence calculus and `preservationKind` vocabulary, verbatim.
- The PROJECTIONS-registry disciplines: register-or-emit-nothing, preservation derived not declared.
- Greenfield: no compat shims in the canonical core; prior dialect versions are frozen generated artifacts.
- No optionality: deterministic estimator as gate; real-tokenizer matrix on a `maint-` lane; hard-fail named failure classes, never silent repair.

## Flagship acceptance scenarios (the depth bar)

1. **Round-trip:** GMN-1 parse∘expand over a bundle sample is semantically identical to the GMN-0 source dataset modulo its ledger entry — the gate is medium-independent.
2. **Token economy:** a claim batch in GMN-1 achieves a ledgered token reduction vs Turtle and JSON-LD under the deterministic estimator.
3. **Symbology coverage:** glyph coverage gate green over all three grounding layers with zero confusables/collisions.
4. **Transport:** per-corpus zstd dictionaries beat dictionary-less zstd on small-record corpora; envelope-declared `dict_id`; byte-identical decompression.
5. **In-dialect repair:** LLM-emitted malformed GMN-1 yields a named failure class returned as a GMN `@err` record — never silent repair.
6. **Compaction honesty:** a GMN-2 compaction is stored as a new provenance-linked claim; sources intact and retrievable.
7. **Primer-card teachability:** a fresh model given only the generated ~500-token primer achieves a gated AST-validity rate on held-out emission tasks.

## Subissues

Blocker chain: S1 blocks S2–S4 and S6; S2–S4 block S6's glyph-lexicon derivation; S5 is independent once S1's envelope contract lands.

- [ ] #1372 — S1: lang: GMN dialect specification IN lang: (SignSystem/Script/Orthography, gmeow:gmn* graft module, GMN-0/1/2 contract, versioning, gates)
- [ ] #1373 — S2: logic: glyph enrichment — operator symbology plane
- [ ] #1374 — S3: math: glyph enrichment — mathematical symbology plane
- [ ] #1375 — S4: lang: glyph enrichment — linguistic symbology plane
- [ ] #1376 — S5: gts/pipeline: machine-compression medium — per-corpus zstd dictionaries + packet envelope
- [ ] #1377 — S6: pipeline/rust: GMN-1 projection via the lang PROJECTIONS registry — graph-derived writer/parser, round-trip gate, token metrics, training-corpus emitter

## Ground rules

- Author in the DSL, not generated artifacts. Every hard rule maps to a gate + a named failure class.
- No optionality, no feature gates, no degraded fallbacks; missing required things are HARD FAILs.
- Deterministic, byte-stable outputs everywhere; the superset law holds over every new artifact.
- Rust-first; **no Python**.
- Design doc (EPIC source-of-truth): [`docs/design/1371-gmeow-dialects.md`](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/paudley/1371-gmeow-dialects/docs/design/1371-gmeow-dialects.md) on branch `paudley/1371-gmeow-dialects`. No implementation begins until child issues are approved.
