title: EPIC: GMEOW dialects — GMN model notation (GMN-0/1/2) + ontology-native symbology + zstd-dictionary transport

body:
### Thesis

The pipeline is single-carrier (`docs/PIPELINE_SPINE.md`): every stage enriches one in-memory `PipelineBundle` fed from RDF sources. Therefore every failure, warning, suggestion, and informational event the build produces is **context-bound** — it is *about* some RDF source context (an authored file:line, a focus node, a named graph, a GTS wire coordinate) and *emitted by* some stage. And because every stage is a morphism (parse: bytes→graph; project: logic→OWL; reason: EDB→IDB), every such event is a **witness of that morphism's defect or partiality**. Today this one concept is fractured across:

- 9+ hand-written error enums (`PipelineError`, `BundleError`, `TranscodeError`, `DocsError`, `MaterializeError`, `ExplainError`, `DiagnosticsConfigError`, string-newtypes in logic-compile, PyO3-local enums);
- ~800 `Result<_, String>` signatures (logic ~228, pipeline ~166, logic-compile ~127, validate ~88, …) that flatten cause chains at every hop (~480 `map_err` in pipeline alone);
- a dozen bespoke accumulators (`LintReport{errors,warnings}`, bare `Vec<Finding>`, `CertificationVerdict`, `GateResult`, `Advisory`, …) each re-inventing severity buckets;
- `gmeow_diagnostics::Report` — the good model — fed by only **two** stages into `graph/diagnostics`;
- the projection loss ledger, carried separately from the diagnostics that are its siblings;
- ad-hoc `eprintln!`-style logging that never reaches the carrier at all.

This epic replaces all of that with **one substrate**: a single diagnostic value that is simultaneously (a) the error payload that propagates through `?`, (b) the finding that accumulates in the carrier, (c) the witness node a later pass can annotate or reason over, and (d) the log event. Severity is graded data; **fatality is a policy decision at the emission site, not a property of the kind** — the same parse defect is fatal at the DAG-load boundary (`Err(…)?`) and collectable during a corpus sweep (`ledger.push`). A subtle logic warning in a reasoning step never aborts; advice is attached by another pass afterwards. All of it rides the same substrate in the carrier and exits through the same projections (SARIF 2.1.0, JSON, HTML, text, `gmeow:` RDF).

### The formal spine (normative for the design)

1. **Witness structure.** A `Diag` is a node in a **derivation/provenance DAG**: its antecedents are other `Diag`s and/or cited quads. The anyhow-style linear context chain is the degenerate (single-parent) case of the same edge set. Reasoning-derived findings reuse `crates/logic/src/explain.rs` (world-scoped reifier indexing, cycle-guarded DFS, deterministic cited-IRI ordering) as the DAG engine — no second implementation.
2. **Grading lattice + one policy morphism.** `(severity × category × standpoint)` forms a bounded lattice; gate fatality is a single monotone up-set over it — ONE policy function `grade → {fatal, collected}`, not ~480 scattered `== Error` tests. "Advisory never gates" and "`PermittedEpistemicConflict` never gates" become theorems of the up-set, enforced in exactly one place. Default grades come from the existing registries (`crates/validate/src/codes.rs`, `gmeow:ruleSeverity` binding/advisory in `crates/pipeline/src/stages/rule_severity.rs`) — no new interner.
3. **Loss unification (Principle 17).** The projection loss ledger and the diagnostic ledger are the same structure: parse defects, projection losses (purrdf `RdfLoss`), and reasoning findings are all graded witnesses, sharing the preservation-judgment vocabulary (mnemomorphic / well-behaved / lossy). `ProjectionLoss` stops being a bolt-on category beside an independent ledger.
4. **Logic-grounded algebra (maximal dogfooding).** The Rust model stays canonical (the substrate must report on input too broken to parse — existing doctrine, `slices/core/diagnostics/docs.md`), but the *laws* — severity ordering, the fatality up-set, category→gating — are authored as `logic:` axioms in the diagnostics slice so the reasoner verifies the policy morphism. `FindingCategory` already mirrors `logic:FindingCategory`; this extends the mirror to the ordering and gating laws. Grounding (Principle 19): finding/suggestion prose grounds in `lang:` forms; the severity ordinal structure grounds in `math:`.
5. **Reasoner-derived meta-findings.** Because findings are content-addressed RDF nodes in a provenance DAG, root-cause clustering ("these 12 SHACL violations trace to one missing `owl:imports`") is a *derived* meta-finding produced by a logic rule — not per-accumulator aggregation code.

### What is preserved (the custom goodness — normative)

From `gmeow_diagnostics` (`crates/diagnostics/src/{model,render}.rs`), carried over verbatim, not reinvented:

- `Severity{Error,Warning,Note,Info}` with alias parsing, `sarif_level()`, sort rank; gate semantics = no Error findings; exit codes via `cli_core::exit_code`.
- `FindingCategory` — the 8-way KIND axis orthogonal to severity, mirroring `logic:FindingCategory`.
- `Location` — physical (`path,line,column`) + logical + GTS wire coords (`gts_term_id/quad_index/reifier_id/frame_index/segment_index`).
- `Rule` + the validate code registry + `gmeow:ruleSeverity` grading.
- `DiagnosticAttribution` (slice IRI + role) — S5 provenance.
- Content fingerprints (`gmeowFindingHash/v2`) and deterministic ordering.
- All five renderers, including GitHub code-scanning hygiene (repo-relative physicalLocation, synthetic fallback anchor, IRI→logicalLocation diversion) and the RDF projection into `https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/graph/diagnostics`.
- The **standpoint/deontic advice structure**: suggestions are not flat strings — `crates/validate/src/advisory.rs` already models advice as a perspectival claim from a `gmeow:Standpoint` with a deontic modality (`AdvisoryProjection{finding, claim}`). The substrate's advice slots fold `AdvisoryClaim` in; advice attached by a later pass MUST carry its vantage (P9).

### Architecture

#### A. The value type — `Diag` (one word, context-bound, a witness)

```rust
pub struct Diag(Box<DiagInner>);   // one machine word; Result<T, Diag> costs nothing over T
struct DiagInner {
    grade: Grade,                  // severity × category × standpoint (lattice point)
    code: Code,                    // interned, registry-checked stable code
    message: String,
    frames: Vec<Frame>,            // context frames (linear antecedent chain)
    antecedents: Vec<DiagRef>,     // DAG edges: findings/quads this witnesses from
    source: Option<BoxedSource>,   // live std::error::Error chain (in-process only, §B3)
    at: SourceContext,
    attributions: Vec<DiagnosticAttribution>,
    advice: Vec<AdvisoryClaim>,    // standpoint-bearing, append-only
    tags: Vec<String>,
}
pub struct SourceContext {
    location: Location,            // path:line:col + GTS coords (existing type)
    graph: Option<Iri>,            // named graph the event is about (absent = honest)
    focus: Option<Term>,           // focus node (absent = honest)
    stage: StageId,                // REQUIRED on the ledger path (see §B4)
}
```

**Representation (normative).** The ledger is a **hash-consed, append-only arena DAG**: `Vec<DiagNode>` arena + `HashMap<Fingerprint, DiagRef>` intern table; `DiagRef(NonZeroU32)` handles (`#[repr(transparent)]`, niche-optimized so `Option<DiagRef>` is free); DAG edges are `Box<[DiagRef]>` handle slices, never owned children. Consequences, by construction rather than by code:

- *Cloning a projection path* = copying a `Vec<DiagRef>` root set over the shared arena — O(roots), zero node copies. Multiple down-projection paths with different loss profiles mint new witness nodes whose antecedents point at the SAME shared upstream handles (persistent structural sharing; no `Clone` of nodes exists).
- *Dedup = content addressing = identity*: hash-consing on the fingerprint means inserting the same witness twice yields the same handle; the deterministic-dedup invariant is the representation, not a fold-time pass (same content-addressed-IR discipline as the logic crate; ordering from the explicit lexical sort key, never derived `Ord`).
- *Parallel stages*: no concurrent structure — each stage appends to its own ledger shard; the presenter merges shards in the total order (stage id + fingerprint). Determinism is scheduler-independent by construction.
- *No `Arc`*: the arena gives cheaper sharing than `Arc<DiagInner>` (u32 handles vs pointer+refcount), full cache locality, and trivially deterministic serialization (indices are a stable topological encoding).
- *Lifecycle*: the boxed `Diag` (Result path) and the arena `DiagNode` are two phases of one datum — a live `Diag` is **absorbed** (interned → `DiagRef`) when collected or cited as an antecedent. Construction paths are `#[cold]`/`#[inline(never)]` (anyhow lesson: keep the happy path hot).
- *Advanced-Rust levers specified*: bit-packed `Grade` lattice point (meet/join = AND/OR; the fatality up-set test = one mask compare), interned `Code(NonZeroU32)` into the registry, `Cow<'static, str>` context frames (static context never allocates), lazy format-args capture in `diag!` for filtered Info-grade events (the tracing lesson). Optional, implementer's call: branded invariant lifetimes on `DiagRef<'ledger>` (generativity pattern) to make cross-ledger handle confusion a compile error.
- *purrdf at the boundary, not the core*: `Term`/`Iri` for focus/graph, `RdfDiagnostic` ingestion, span-table blobs via the blob store, lowering to `RdfDataset` quads; the fingerprint scheme aligns with purrdf-core's content-id machinery so a finding's IRI and its blob-store identity are one scheme. The hot in-memory structure is NOT RDF quads — no triple-building on the `?` path.

thiserror's lesson: structural failure classes that today justify enum variants (`ResourceMismatch{stage,rdf,rust}`, `CacheMismatch`, …) become typed payload structs implementing a `DiagKind` trait (code + category + Display co-located; hand-written or via one `macro_rules!` — no proc-macro dep). `Diag::downcast_ref::<T>()` recovers them, so match-on-variant call sites keep working.

#### B. Propagation ergonomics (anyhow lessons, no anyhow) — with the sharp edges resolved

1. `pub type Result<T, E = Diag> = std::result::Result<T, E>;` — bare `?` everywhere via the blanket `From<E: Error + Send + Sync + 'static>`. **Coherence rule:** the blanket impl is the ONLY `From`; `RdfDiagnostic`, kinds, and reports enter via named constructors (`Diag::from_rdf`, `kind.into_diag()`). (anyhow compiles only because it makes the same choice.)
2. `ResultExt`: `.ctx("…")`, `.with_ctx(|| …)`, `.at(loc)`, `.for_focus(term)`, `.grade(Warning)` — replaces the ~480 pipeline `map_err(|e| format!("…: {e}"))` shapes. `bail!`/`ensure!`/`diag!` macros for emission. Display = outermost message; `{:#}` walks frames + source chain (and, for derivation-backed findings, the DAG via explain.rs).
3. **Serialization boundary (soundness):** the live `dyn Error` source chain exists in-process only. At the cache/carrier edge every `Diag` is **lowered**: the source chain becomes deterministic structured frames (code + rendered message), and ONLY the lowered form is content-addressed and pinned. Fresh and cache-replayed diagnostics are therefore byte-identical by construction.
4. **Fatality = call-site policy:** `return Err(diag)` short-circuits; `ledger.push(diag)` accumulates; promotion/demotion goes through the ONE policy morphism (§spine 2). A pre-carrier `Diag` (CLI arg/config errors) uses a distinct constructor without a `StageId` — modeled as a different entry point, not an `Option` that leaks optionality into the ledger path.

#### C. RDF source context from purrdf ≥0.3.1

- Parse failures: `purrdf::RdfDiagnostic{severity,code,message,detail,location,losses}` → `Diag::from_rdf`; `RdfLocation{path,line,column,gts_*}` is shape-compatible with `Location`; `losses` become `ProjectionLoss`-graded child witnesses (§spine 3).
- Parsed content: source-load stages parse authored `slices/` with `ParseOptions{track_source_spans: true}` → `SpanTable` (subject lexical key → line/col). Span tables attach to the carrier **as digest-pinned blobs keyed by authored graph** (reusing the blob store + pin-on-attach; they ride cache replay, no side-channel). Any later stage — SHACL, logic compile, reasoning, lints — joins a focus node back to its authored `file:line` when minting a `Diag`. This is what lets a *reasoning* warning point at the slice line that authored the offending axiom.
- **Span policy is a fixed rule, not a knob**: authored `slices/`/`dsl/` sources = spans ON, always; bulk `imports/` = spans OFF, always (their subjects are not human-fixable lines; honest absence, and .goals' "trim only at exit" is satisfied because no exit consumer of import spans exists). No per-call configuration surface. Memory discipline: span tables are dropped from the carrier after the last consuming stage (declared consumption, like any dataflow edge), with a test on the largest slice (25s-budget guard — the prose-lift corpus precedent).
- Non-span formats (RDF/XML, TriX, HexTuples) keep the synthetic-anchor discipline; absence is honest data, never guessed (epistemic-shape rule).
- Note: the span machinery shipped in purrdf 0.3.0; 0.3.1 is a formatting release. This epic pins ≥0.3.1.

#### C2. Maximal automatic capture — nothing load-bearing is hand-typed

The goal state for a rendered finding is fully self-describing: `source<line 12, quad 2, object position in file x> · locus<primary reasoning pass, stage-reason, level 4/9> · observation<found X, expected Y> · references<spec §, internal docs page>`. Each channel is captured **automatically**, at the layer that owns the fact — emission sites supply only the code and the observation:

- **Pipeline locus (ambient, zero per-site plumbing).** The scheduler already knows everything about *where* the build is; the ledger shard it hands each stage carries a `PipelineLocus{stage: StageId, impl_key, phase, level, position, pass}` (phase = the human name, e.g. "primary reasoning pass"; level/position = topological coordinates from the loaded DAG; pass = iteration for fixpoint stages). Every `diag!`/`ledger.push` stamps it implicitly — the tracing-span lesson: context is ambient, not threaded by hand. Because the DAG is dogfooded RDF, the locus links to the `gmeow:PipelineStage` individual — the finding's position in the build is itself ontology-grounded.
- **Emitting-code provenance for free.** `ResultExt`/`bail!`/`diag!` use `#[track_caller]`/`Location::caller()` so every witness records the Rust `file:line` that minted it (renderer-visible under `properties.gmeow.emitter`) — no macro user ever types it, and "which gate produced this?" is never archaeology.
- **Sub-statement source coordinates.** `Location` gains the statement-level channel the GTS coords already hint at: quad index within the source graph plus a `TermRole` (subject/predicate/object/graph — the "attribute") so a finding can say *quad 2, object position*. The SpanTable join fills line/col; the validate/reason engines fill quad+role (SHACL results already know the value/path; reasoning citations already carry reifiers). Absent channels stay honestly absent.
- **Structured observation (rustc's expected/found lesson).** `observed: Term|Literal` / `expected: Option<Term|Literal|ShapeRef>` are first-class typed slots beside `message`, not prose — so "suboptimal X, should be Y" is machine-actionable (diffable, remediation input for #1310, SARIF `message.arguments`), and message text stays out of fingerprints without losing the substance.
- **References resolve from the registry, never at call sites.** Each `Code` in the registry carries its reference set: external spec/help URIs (existing `help_uri`) plus internal anchors — the `gmeow:ValidationRule` individual, the generated docs page for the governing term, design-doc paths. Renderers join code → references at exit; emission sites cannot ship stale links because they never contain any. New codes without a registry entry are a HARD FAIL (invariant 3), so the reference channel is total.
- **"Fully reasoned-about" at exit.** The final render of any Error-grade finding includes: the derivation walk (explain.rs DAG → cited axioms/rules), the policy-morphism verdict trace (which lattice point, which up-set test made it gate), and the full locus chain. A finding the system cannot explain to that depth is itself an `IncompleteCheck`-category witness — the substrate reports on its own blind spots.

#### D. The carrier ledger — same substrate, in the spine

- `DiagLedger` becomes a first-class carrier member (peer of the blob store and provenance sidecar): append-only, stage-attributed, content-addressed.
- **Determinism under parallel scheduling:** ledger order is a TOTAL deterministic order — `sort_key` extended with `StageId` and the content fingerprint as tiebreakers; identical witnesses dedup by fingerprint. The byte-stable superset gate must hold under any nextest/scheduler interleaving.
- **Fingerprint discipline:** the v2 fingerprint and the `finding/{fingerprint}` IRIs key on `(code, category, source-context anchor, focus)` — NEVER message text or context frames (wording tweaks must not churn goldens or orphan attached advice; same rule that already keeps `FindingCategory` out of `sort_key`).
- Every stage may contribute; the presenter's fold generalizes from today's two-producer union to a keyed union over all stages' contributions, still emitted once into `graph/diagnostics` (transform-once razor), still a registered fanout member that round-trips through `gmeow.gts`. SARIF/RDF enrichment from spans lands with this phase.
- Pin-on-attach applies: a stage's ledger contribution is digest-pinned with its product, so cached stage replays replay their diagnostics (closing today's silent-drop gap).
- **Annotation by later passes:** advice passes attach standpoint-bearing `AdvisoryClaim`s / remediation / explain-skeleton quads that *reference* existing finding IRIs — append-only enrichment, ordinary RDF. #1310 rides here.

#### E. Logging subsumption

Events *about* the build's subject matter are `Note`/`Info` witnesses — into the ledger, hence into the bundle, queryable like everything else. Emission macro `diag!(ledger, Info, code, "…"; at = loc)`; console sink via `cli-core` `Reporter`/`ConsoleMode` (existing summarized/advisory text modes), replacing scattered `eprintln!`. Two honest carve-outs, drawn precisely:

- `transient` events (operational chatter: thread scheduling, progress ticks) render to console only. `transient` is a **closed, enumerated category** — not a per-call escape hatch. Boundary vs Principle 18: perf timings destined for the release-evidence lane are NOT transient — they are carried as data, as the Constitution already requires; only chatter with no downstream consumer is transient.
- The substrate works before a carrier exists (CLI/config errors) via the pre-carrier constructor (§B4).

Subsuming any remaining general-purpose (non-context-bound) logging is a child of this epic, sequenced last — context-bound events, the requirement, are core.

#### F. Boundaries

- **PyO3:** the documented exception contract holds (`MaterializeError::Parse`→`ValueError`, `Chase`→`RuntimeError`): kinds carry an exception-class hint; one shared `diag_to_pyerr` replaces per-crate routers. Reports keep crossing as data (`PyReport`).
- **CLI:** exit codes stay report-driven via `cli_core::exit_code`; `gmeow-dev feedback`'s fold surface becomes uniform since every gate returns the substrate's `Report`.
- **SARIF:** renderer contract unchanged, fed richer physical locations (spans) and the frame/DAG context in `properties.gmeow.context`; SARIF `fixes` unlock with #1310 (phase 5 of this epic).
- **Downstream consumers unlocked** (named children): LSP `publishDiagnostics` for live slice-authoring feedback (spans make it nearly free); `gmeow explain <finding-iri>` walking the derivation DAG via explain.rs; SPARQL competency queries + MCP agentic tools over the diagnostic graph ("all findings attributed to slice X", "everything tracing to this parse error").

### Hard invariants

1. Deterministic output everywhere: total ledger order (stage + fingerprint tiebreakers), content-addressed dedup, byte-stable RDF/`.nq` under any parallel interleaving.
2. The Rust model is canonical; RDF is a projection (must report on unparsable input).
3. No-optionality: unknown severity token, unregistered code, ledger attachment contradicting its pinned digest, or a carrier-path `Diag` without a `StageId` = HARD FAIL; missing spans/focus/graph are honest absence, never guessed.
4. Gate fatality is computed by the ONE policy morphism; advisory-tier and `PermittedEpistemicConflict` never gate — as theorems, tested once.
5. Source chains are never pre-flattened in-process; lowering to structured frames happens exactly once, at the cache/carrier serialization edge.
6. Fingerprints/IRIs never key on message text or context frames.
7. No new proc-macro or error-crate dependencies; cli-core's lone thiserror use is retired.
8. Typed domain report structs are **stateless views over the ledger** — they hold no independent findings store.
9. 25s per-test budget + nextest grouping respected; span tracking never on the bulk-import path; span-table memory bounded with declared drop points.
10. GitHub code-scanning SARIF constraints (physical location, repo-relative URIs, fingerprints) keep passing — the upload lane is load-bearing.

### Sequencing (dependency order)

0. **Base**: purrdf ≥0.3.1 / edition 2024 (#1330, parent #1314).
1. **Crate bootstrap**: `crates/errors` (`gmeow_errors`) absorbing `crates/diagnostics` (model + renderers move; `gmeow_native.diagnostics` import paths updated; no compat shim). Adds `Diag`, `Grade` lattice + policy morphism, `DiagKind`, `SourceContext`, `ResultExt`, `bail!`/`ensure!`/`diag!`, blanket `From` (+ coherence rule), downcast, `{:#}`, `Diag::from_rdf`, lowering (§B3), fingerprint discipline.
2. **Carrier ledger**: `DiagLedger` on the carrier; every-stage contribution; ambient `PipelineLocus` stamping via the scheduler-issued shard; presenter fold generalization + SARIF/RDF span enrichment; cached-replay diagnostics; span-table blobs at source-load with the fixed span policy + drop points.
3. **Pipeline adoption**: `PipelineError`/`BundleError`/`TranscodeError` variants become `DiagKind`s; ~480 pipeline `map_err` sites collapse onto `ResultExt`; stage `run` returns `gmeow_errors::Result`; goldens re-blessed where messages gain context (drift owned).
4. **Producer sweep + loss unification**: validate lints, logic verdict/ledger accumulators, scoreboard gates, advisories emit the substrate directly (domain reports become stateless views); the projection loss ledger merges into the witness structure (§spine 3); diagnostics-slice `logic:` axioms for the grading algebra + `lang:`/`math:` grounding.
5. **Annotation passes**: content-addressed advice attachment (standpoint-bearing `AdvisoryClaim`s); #1310 remediation + explain-skeleton enrichment; reasoner-derived root-cause meta-findings.
6. **Consumers + long tail**: LSP publishDiagnostics; `gmeow explain <finding>`; MCP/SPARQL surfaces; console sink replaces ad-hoc eprintln; per-crate `Result<_, String>` migration children (logic, logic-compile, validate, docs, conformance, music, CLIs); retire cli-core thiserror; general-purpose logging subsumption.

Child issues are filed per numbered item as work starts.

### Non-goals

- No behavioral change to gate outcomes: same errors fail, same advisories don't.
- No RDF-canonical diagnostics (doctrine unchanged — must report on unparsable input).
- No external error-handling dependencies.
- The conformance-harness verdict machinery is a separate engine and is not replaced here.

### Enhancements considered and declined

- **anyhow/thiserror as dependencies** — declined: neither can carry `SourceContext`/the carrier ledger; subsuming their ergonomics into a context-bound type is the SUBSUME+EXTEND+ENHANCE route, and the house convention (`crates/pipeline/src/error.rs:4-9`) already bans the deps.
- **RDF as the canonical diagnostic model** — declined: violates the report-on-unparsable-input doctrine; the vocabulary stays authored in the slice, instances stay projections.

### Related

#1310 (advice/remediation — rides phase 5) · #1330 / #1314 (purrdf 0.3.1 base) · `docs/PIPELINE_SPINE.md` (carrier doctrine) · `slices/core/diagnostics/docs.md` + `module.ttl` (canonical-model doctrine + vocabulary) · `crates/logic/src/explain.rs` (derivation-DAG engine) · `crates/validate/src/advisory.rs` (standpoint/deontic advice) · `crates/validate/src/codes.rs` + `crates/pipeline/src/stages/rule_severity.rs` (code/severity registries) · `crates/pipeline/src/error.rs` (house error convention this generalizes) · `docs/APPLIED_CATEGORY_THEORY/` (morphism-witness framing, Principle 17).

Tracking meta-epic for the outward face of the projection doctrine: **every prior formalism is a lowering of one `logic:` IR**, on a lattice of four distinct relations. This is the completion of Principle 17 — the canonical statement is in [`LOGIC-META-SEMANTICS.md` § the outward face](slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-META-SEMANTICS.md#the-outward-face-every-prior-formalism-placed-on-one-lattice).

## The lattice (four relations, deliberately not one "projects-to")

| Relation | Members | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `logic: ─isBuiltAtop→` | RDF 1.2 | ✅ substrate — never projected |
| `logic: ─isSupersetOf→` | OWL, RDFS, gUFO, UFO, **SKOS** | ◑ OWL/RDFS/gUFO lifted+projected today; SKOS is the gap |
| `logic: ─downProjectsLossilyTo→` | SHACL, ShEx | ⏳ #1197 |
| `logic: + mappings ─derives→` | SSSOM, EDOAL, FnO | ✅ built; being sourced from slice linkage in the correspondence epic |

## The shared foundation

Completing `adapter.rs`'s lift of the authored semantic surface into the IR feeds **all three** lower relations at once (restriction/cardinality lift → validation; SKOS lift → superset gap + alignment; one generalized purity gate). That is the blocker node.

## Children (sub-issues)

- [ ] #1199 — **foundation**: complete the adapter's semantic-surface lift (restrictions/cardinality) — *blocks the rest*
- [ ] #1200 — lift SKOS (annotations + `skos:*Match`); close the `isSupersetOf` gap
- [ ] #1201 — generalize the projection-purity gate to the whole surface
- [ ] #1197 — EPIC: SHACL/ShEx as the validation down-projection (V1–V4)
- [ ] #1202 — EPIC: derive `logic:Correspondence` from slice linkage; SSSOM/EDOAL/FnO fall out

## Related

- #1087 — Correspondence Calculus (the alignment leg's canonical object).
- #1195 — ADL2/OPT consumer, downstream of #1199 + #1197.

## Definition of done

RDF 1.2 is the only non-projected floor; OWL/RDFS/SKOS/gUFO are lifted-and-projected; SHACL/ShEx are derived validation surfaces; SSSOM/EDOAL/FnO are derived alignment surfaces; one purity gate forbids any hand-authored generated-surface construct; every edge carries a loss-ledger judgment; full `make check` green.

Tracking epic for making **SHACL Core and ShEx generated lossy projections of the `logic:` canon**, derived from the constraint axioms already authored in each slice — the shape-surface peer of the SHACL-AF computation surface. Applies Principles 17 / 4 / 12 to validation, exactly as the Correspondence Calculus (#1087) applies them to alignment.

Design doc: [`slices/grounding/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md`](slices/grounding/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md) (peer of `LOGIC-SHACL-AF.md`; cross-linked from `LOGIC.md` / `LOGIC-IR.md`).

## Status (triaged 2026-07-07)

V1 (#1191) and V2 (#1192) are **CLOSED** and their machinery is live: `ValidationShapeIr` is constructed (`crates/logic-compile/src/ir.rs` — `validation_shapes` / `with_validation_shapes`), and the derived-shape projection landed with byte/well-formedness/dogfood goldens for shacl-core/shex/shacl-af (#1401). The original "dead variant / never constructed" gap is closed.

## The remaining gap

- **21 hand-authored `slices/**/shapes.ttl` still exist** — the second source of truth Principle 4 forbids is still standing until V4 retires them behind equivalence proofs.
- The purity gate (`check_projection_shape_purity`, `crates/validate/src/repo_static.rs`) seals only the `sh:sparql` procedural fragment; the **declarative `NodeShape`/`PropertyShape` seal is explicitly deferred in-code** — V3's remit.
- **`conformance/validation/` does not exist** (only `conformance/logic/`) — the validation conformance category V3 promises is unbuilt.
- Structural ShEx (`write_shex` from the vocabulary FoldView) is not yet retired in favor of the derived lowering — V4.

## Children (dependency order)

- [x] #1191 — V1: derive `ValidationShapeIr` from existing slice constraint axioms (closed-world reading)
- [x] #1192 — V2: project the derived shape to SHACL Core + ShEx (one lowering, per-target loss ledger)
- [ ] #1193 — V3: shape-half purity gate (declarative seal) + carrier/gts wiring + `conformance/validation/` category — **in flight**
- [ ] #1194 — V4: equivalence-before-deletion — retire hand-authored `shapes.ttl` + structural ShEx

## Related

- **#1087** — Correspondence Calculus: sibling doctrine; a `logic:Correspondence`'s validation law (`π_target(d(g)) ⊨ shapes`) is discharged by a shape this epic projects.
- **#1195** — Full ADL2/OPT → `logic:`/SHACL constraint lowering (downstream **consumer**): an ADL constraint lowers to a `logic:` axiom → derived validation shape → SHACL via this machinery. Must not build a parallel constraint-derivation path.
- **#1201** — generalizing the purity gate to the whole semantic-vocabulary surface builds on V3's shape-half seal.

## Definition of done

- Zero hand-authored `sh:NodeShape` / `sh:PropertyShape` in `slices/` / `shapes/` / `dsl/`; the shape-half purity gate enforces it and the tree passes.
- Every `generated/shapes/*.ttl` and `gmeow.shex` is a provable projection of authored `logic:` constraint axioms; `check-generated` green; `gmeow.gts` carries them via the typed `Shacl` / `Shex` lookaside.
- SHACL and ShEx lower from the **same** derived node (cannot drift); each declares an honest preservation claim; the overclaim gate is green.
- Full `make check` green after integrating current `main`.

body:
## Summary

Retire the second sources of truth: delete the hand-authored slice/root SHACL shapes and the structural ShEx export, once the `logic:`-projected surfaces (V2/V3) reproduce them. Greenfield, equivalence-before-deletion.

Design doc: [`slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md`](slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md). Depends on: **V3** (gate + wiring + conformance in place).

## Scope

- **Equivalence-before-deletion.** The 15 slice `shapes.ttl` + 3 root `shapes/*.ttl` are the golden oracle. The V2 projector must regenerate them **graph-isomorphically** before the hand-authored files are removed. Author the equivalent `logic:` validation shapes (via the V1 frontend), diff-prove parity, then delete the hand-authored Turtle.
- **Retire the structural ShEx.** Remove the vocabulary-`FoldView`-derived `write_shex` (`crates/pipeline/src/stages/export.rs:2273`) once the IR-fed ShEx projector (V2) reproduces `gmeow.shex`; keep byte/graph parity as the deletion gate.
- **Reconcile the two existing SHACL stages.** `crates/pipeline/src/stages/frame_shapes.rs` (from `gmeow:requiresFrame`) and `result_shapes.rs` (from `logic:ResultShape`) already emit `generated/shapes/*.ttl`. Fold them in as the validation-shape projector's first realized fragment rather than leaving a parallel emit path — or explicitly document why a given stage stays separate.

## Out of scope / longer arc (do NOT bundle here)

- Retiring the standalone `crates/shacl` engine to a conformance oracle by routing constraint **checking** onto the relational-core lowering. Note it in the design doc's runtime-relationship section; it is a separate track.

## Acceptance

- Zero hand-authored `sh:NodeShape` / `sh:PropertyShape` remain in `slices/`, `shapes/`, `dsl/` (the V3 purity gate now enforces this — this part makes the tree actually pass it).
- `gmeow.shex` and every `generated/shapes/*.ttl` are provably projections of authored `logic:` validation shapes; `check-generated` green.
- No parallel SHACL emit path: frame/result shapes are either folded into the projector or documented as intentional exceptions with a `logic:formalizes` back-reference.
- Full `make check` green after integrating current `main`.

---
**Series:** SHACL/ShEx validation-projection (V1–V4). Depends on #1193.
